summary.intent: Get PR #470 (callisto repo) passing CI by fixing a clippy failure and a merge conflict, then work out why simple verification mistakes keep happening and how to prevent them in this repo and in other repos generally.
summary.outcome: Fixed the clippy failure (moved function above test module) and merged main to resolve the versioning.md conflict with #471; pushed a signed merge commit and ran the repo's just recipes (pre-push, doc-check, lint, test) with exit 0. Produced a root-cause analysis and a lightweight proposal (AGENTS.md line, global CLAUDE.md lines, hook-chain repair), all awaiting user approval; the Claude-hook idea was rejected as too heavy.

repo: CI runs `just doc-check`, `just lint` (workspace-wide `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`), and `just test` (nextest); `just ci` is the full suite (coverage, audit, zizmor) and `just pre-push` runs format check plus clippy.
CONTRIBUTING.md and AGENTS.md say to run `just ci` and keep `just pre-push` clean.

The git pre-push hook appears dead: Entire's wrappers chain pre-push -> pre-push.pre-entire -> pre-push.pre-entire-brain, which ends the chain and never calls the original `just pre-push` backup. This is an inference from files and push output, not proven by running the hook.
Entire has no found command to repair its hook chain; `just hooks` may be re-wrapped by Entire on its next run.
#470 and #471 both added bullets to docs/architecture/versioning.md, causing a merge conflict; resolved by keeping both bullets.
Clippy lint `items_after_test_module` fires when a function is placed after the test module (release_preview.rs).

code.finding: Conflict region between #470 and #471 where both PRs added bullets; resolved by keeping both.
`group_operations` was appended after the test module, triggering clippy `items_after_test_module`; moved above it in commit 9966e06b6.

workflow: Judge checks by exit code (`echo exit=$?`), never by `tail -1` or `grep -c` of output; `grep -vc ' 0 failed'` returns 0 on a compile failure because no result lines exist, so a broken build looks green.
Run the repo's own CI-equivalent commands (just recipes, or the commands in the CI workflow) instead of ad-hoc cargo invocations on a subset of crates.
After pushing, verify each commit's signature (`verification.reason` is `valid`) and read `gh pr checks`.
Don't put claims in PRs or specs (e.g. 'offline, no registry lookup') without a test behind them; a fixture with no `origin` hid real CI behavior.
Edit scripts should be all-or-nothing: compute all replacements first, then write once, to avoid half-applied edits.
User prefers lightweight text-based guidance (AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md lines) over Claude hooks, which they consider too heavy.

friction: Unsigned commits blocked PRs from merging and were only noticed when the user hit it.
Clippy failure on #470 was missed because the local run printed a log pointer instead of 'No issues found' and was read past.
Rustdoc failure on #464 because only clippy was run locally, not `just doc-check`.
Test-count grep check gave a false green on a broken build.
A false 'offline' claim in a PR and spec was caught by a reviewer.
Edit scripts left half-applied work twice.
Many interleaved requests led to batched steps and shortcuts.
Entire's hook wrapping silently disables the repo's pre-push gate.
